paragraphs: Sparse autoencoders try to explain language model activity through features that people can interpret. Increasing the number of available features often divides broad concepts into narrower ones: a mathematics feature might separate into algebra and geometry. This paper asks whether that apparent hierarchy provides a dependable account of what the model represents.

The authors identify feature absorption: a broad feature sometimes stays inactive even when its concept is present, because narrower child features take over its representation. A feature that appears to represent one clean concept can therefore give a misleading picture of when that concept occurs. The paper connects this behavior to the pressure to use fewer active features when the underlying concepts form a hierarchy.

The authors introduce an absorption metric and investigate hundreds of language model autoencoders. Their findings suggest that changing feature counts or sparsity alone does not resolve the problem. The implication is that interpreting a feature requires understanding its relationship with other features, and that robust interpretation may require addressing deeper issues in the sparse decomposition itself.
neurips-2025-a-is-for-absorption-studyin.tldr: Sparse autoencoders can hide broad concepts inside narrower features, undermining the reliability of apparently interpretable features.

paragraphs: In auction-based federated learning, data consumers choose which data owners to work with and how much to bid for their participation. These decisions occur in changing markets, where a fixed bidding rule may respond poorly to new circumstances. RLB-AFL treats bidding as a sequential decision problem that an agent can learn to navigate.

The method adds historical states to a Deep Q-Network so that decisions can reflect the progression of earlier auctions. A second component addresses the fact that any particular auction state may rarely recur. A Gaussian Mixture Model softly groups sequential states, reducing the effective dimensionality of the state space and making exploration and estimation of action values easier.

The authors also modify the exploration policy to balance trying unfamiliar actions with using actions that already appear beneficial. Experiments across six benchmark datasets compare the method with eight existing approaches and report superior performance in average total utility. Together, the components support adaptive bidding by combining market history, more manageable state representations, and a revised approach to exploration.
neurips-2025-a-reinforcement-learning-ba.tldr: RLB-AFL learns adaptive bids for federated learning auctions using auction history, soft state clustering, and an enhanced exploration policy.

paragraphs: Models that combine multiple kinds of input can learn those inputs unevenly. Differences in their ability to represent each modality create competition during training. Existing balancing methods often assess a modality's overall contribution, but that can overlook how its usefulness changes between individual examples and over the course of learning.

CMoB makes these changing contributions the basis of its training strategy. It defines a benefit function using informational uncertainty to assess how the importance of examples evolves. It then uses a causal perspective to quantify modality contributions within individual samples, providing a more detailed view than a single assessment for an entire modality.

During training, these evaluations guide which modalities receive additional optimization. The intended balance includes strengthening important modalities' ability to distinguish examples while improving modalities that remain poorly learned. Experiments across multimodal datasets and learning frameworks report advantages over existing approaches. The contribution is an adaptive way to allocate training effort according to what each modality contributes to particular examples at particular stages.
neurips-2025-cmob-modality-valuation-via.tldr: CMoB balances multimodal training by tracking how individual modalities contribute to each example as learning progresses.

paragraphs: Reasoning from orthographic projections is central to CAD workflows, where precise dimensions and editable parameters matter. Standard 3D reconstruction approaches can lose these properties. Vision-language models offer another route, but supervised fine-tuning can encourage memorization of familiar patterns and leave models struggling with unfamiliar, complex reasoning problems.

CReFT-CAD uses two training stages in a specific order. It first applies reinforcement learning with a curriculum and rewards that account for task difficulty, aiming to build reasoning abilities progressively. Supervised post-tuning then refines instruction following and the extraction of relevant meaning. This separates the development of reasoning behavior from later refinement of how the model interprets and follows requests.

The paper also introduces TriView2CAD, a benchmark containing 200,000 synthetic and 3,000 real-world orthographic projections, precise dimensional annotations, and six interoperable data modalities. Evaluations of leading vision-language models show that CReFT-CAD improves reasoning accuracy and generalization to unfamiliar real-world cases. The training method and benchmark together target the dimensional reasoning needed for practical CAD work.
neurips-2025-creft-cad-boosting-orthogra.tldr: CReFT-CAD combines curriculum-based reinforcement learning with supervised post-tuning to improve CAD projection reasoning and generalization.

paragraphs: Removing an unwanted concept from a text-to-image model can also weaken unrelated generation abilities. CURE addresses this trade-off by directly editing the weights of a pretrained diffusion model. Its procedure requires no retraining, supervision, or iterative optimization, making concept suppression a single calculated model update.

The central component, called the Spectral Eraser, analyzes token embeddings for concepts to remove and concepts to retain. Singular Value Decomposition identifies directions that distinguish those groups, and an orthogonal projection isolates features associated with the unwanted concept. An additional expansion mechanism adjusts selected directions according to their relative significance, controlling how strongly the model forgets while seeking to preserve other attributes.

The authors report that the closed-form procedure performs erasure in two seconds. Comparisons with prior methods show more efficient and thorough removal of targeted styles, objects, identities, and explicit content, with minor damage to original generation ability. The edited models also show improved robustness in red-teaming evaluations. These findings support fast, selective suppression, while retaining the stated trade-off between forgetting and preserving other capabilities.
neurips-2025-cure-concept-unlearning-via.tldr: CURE suppresses unwanted image concepts through a single closed-form weight edit, with reported improvements in efficiency and selectivity.

paragraphs: Foundation models require processing large collections of text, images, video, and audio. Supporting all of these formats introduces demands that traditional data frameworks struggle to meet. Data-Juicer 2.0 provides a system for this work, with more than 100 processing operators covering analysis, synthesis, annotation, and tasks associated with model post-training.

The system combines several ways to express processing work with a runtime that adapts execution to different environments and scales. Users can interact through Python, REST APIs, or conversational commands. Compatibility and targeted optimizations for resources such as Hugging Face datasets and the Ray computing engine help connect those interfaces to existing data and computing infrastructure.

Empirical evaluations demonstrate processing at terabyte scale using more than 10,000 CPU cores. The authors report improvements over the previous version in usability, efficiency, and programmability, alongside adoption in research and products including Alibaba Cloud PAI. The contribution links multimodal processing functionality with execution infrastructure, so that the same system supports both defining data operations and carrying them out at substantial scale.
neurips-2025-data-juicer-2-0-cloud-scale.tldr: Data-Juicer 2.0 combines multimodal processing tools with adaptive execution for foundation-model data workflows at cloud scale.

paragraphs: Simulation-based inference uses synthetic examples from a simulator to infer plausible model parameters from observed data. Typically, this involves training a neural network to estimate a posterior distribution. When simulations are expensive, the number required can become a major obstacle, alongside the work of choosing and tuning the inference network.

NPE-PFN repurposes TabPFN, a pretrained foundation model for tabular data, as a conditional density estimator. It uses an autoregressive formulation to estimate posterior distributions without selecting and training a new inference network for each task. This shifts the inference procedure toward using an already trained general-purpose model with the available simulated examples.

Across benchmark tasks and two complex scientific inverse problems, the method achieves accuracy competitive with current simulation-based approaches. It often needs substantially fewer simulations, with reductions of orders of magnitude in some cases. The authors also report better robustness to model misspecification and show how to use simulation budgets larger than TabPFN's context limit. These findings suggest a practical route to reducing both simulation costs and inference-model development effort.
neurips-2025-effortless-simulation-effic.tldr: NPE-PFN uses pretrained TabPFN for Bayesian inference, often reducing simulation requirements while avoiding task-specific inference-network training.

paragraphs: Language models pass through several training stages, making it difficult to determine how an earlier design choice affects later reasoning performance. EvoLM provides a model suite for examining that process across pretraining, continued pretraining, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning. Its purpose is to make the interactions between stages easier to study systematically.

The authors train more than 100 models from scratch at sizes of one billion and four billion parameters. They examine both language modeling and downstream problem solving, including performance within training domains and generalization beyond them. This breadth connects changes in the underlying language model with their consequences for reasoning tasks.

The study identifies diminishing returns from excessive pretraining and post-training, as well as trade-offs in configuring supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. It emphasizes continued pretraining as a bridge between stages and examines practices for reducing forgetting during domain-specific training. Releasing the models, datasets, and complete training and evaluation pipeline enables other researchers to investigate these findings and the dependencies between training decisions.
neurips-2025-evolm-in-search-of-lost-tra.tldr: EvoLM exposes reasoning-related trade-offs across language-model training stages through a released suite of more than 100 models.

paragraphs: The HiggsML Uncertainty Challenge studies how to measure particle properties when the simulator used for analysis is imperfect. Participants had to report confidence intervals for a Higgs-boson parameter while accounting for systematic uncertainties. The task therefore evaluates how methods express uncertainty about a physical measurement, beyond identifying which simulated collisions contain a signal.

The released dataset contains 280 million simulated proton-proton collision instances with 28 features. These describe collisions as observed at CERN's Large Hadron Collider. Features include particle energy and three-dimensional momentum, together with quantities derived using physics knowledge. Labels distinguish the Higgs events of interest from three sources of background events.

The paper describes leading submissions, including approaches based on contrastive normalising flows and density-ratio estimation through classification. Its permanent dataset release supports continuing comparisons of methods for handling systematic uncertainty. By combining a concrete physical inference task with a large shared dataset, the challenge gives physics and machine learning researchers a common setting for studying reliable measurements under imperfect simulation.
neurips-2025-fair-universe-higgsml-uncer.tldr: The HiggsML challenge provides a large simulation dataset for evaluating confidence intervals that account for systematic uncertainty.

paragraphs: Text-to-video diffusion models can generate visually convincing content while struggling with motion and changing interactions. Common remedies involve retraining or supplying external guidance. FlowMo investigates whether a pretrained model's own intermediate predictions already contain temporal information that can guide it toward more coherent motion during generation.

At each diffusion step, FlowMo compares latent representations of consecutive frames to derive a temporal representation with reduced influence from appearance. It then measures how this representation varies over time within individual patches. That variance supplies a motion-coherence signal, which the method uses to guide sampling toward lower temporal variance.

The method requires neither additional training nor auxiliary inputs, so it can be applied to pretrained video diffusion models through their sampling process. Experiments across multiple models show significant improvements in motion coherence without sacrificing visual quality or alignment with the text prompt. The results indicate that information already present in a model's predictions can provide useful temporal guidance, making motion improvement possible without building a separate conditioning source.
neurips-2025-flowmo-variance-based-flow-.tldr: FlowMo improves generated video motion by guiding sampling with temporal signals extracted from the model's own predictions.

paragraphs: Recovering a detailed 3D person from one ordinary photograph is difficult because body proportions, poses, belongings, and surface appearance vary widely. GeneMAN addresses these challenges using human data from several sources: 3D scans, videos with multiple views, individual photographs, and generated synthetic examples. This collection supports specialized models for human reconstruction.

The framework first trains a human-focused text-to-image diffusion model and a view-conditioned diffusion model. These provide learned guidance about human appearance and 3D structure without relying on a parametric body model such as SMPL. A geometry initialization and sculpting pipeline then uses these priors to recover the person's shape from the input image.

A separate texture pipeline refines appearance successively in latent space and pixel space. Experiments report higher-quality reconstructions than prior leading methods and improved generalization to ordinary photographs. In particular, the system often produces detailed models of people in natural poses with common items across varying body proportions. The approach combines broad human-data coverage with distinct stages for geometric structure and surface detail.
neurips-2025-geneman-generalizable-singl.tldr: GeneMAN combines human-specific diffusion priors and staged refinement to reconstruct detailed 3D people from single photographs.

paragraphs: This paper studies binary classifiers built from continuous piecewise linear functions with a particular geometric structure. Their decision boundaries are starshaped polyhedral sets, which may be nonconvex. The functions are supported on a fixed polyhedral simplicial fan, so the analysis concerns a specified arrangement of linear regions rather than unrestricted classifier architectures.

The authors investigate both what these classifiers can express and how their optimization landscapes are organized. They provide explicit bounds on VC dimension, a measure of classification capacity. For the discrete loss that counts incorrect predictions, they describe sublevel sets—collections of models whose loss stays below a chosen threshold—as chambers in an arrangement of hyperplanes.

They also examine a log-likelihood objective. Here, they establish sufficient conditions for a unique optimum and describe how its geometry changes with the rate parameter of the underlying exponential probability distribution. These results connect the model's geometric restrictions to its capacity and optimization behavior. The uniqueness statement is conditional: the paper supplies conditions that ensure it, rather than asserting uniqueness for every model in the class.
neurips-2025-how-to-learn-a-star-binary-.tldr: The paper characterizes the expressive capacity and loss geometry of classifiers with starshaped polyhedral decision boundaries.

paragraphs: Flexible job-shop scheduling must account for production constraints while allowing operations to be allocated to different machines. Many reinforcement learning methods construct a schedule directly, but may stop short of near-optimal solutions. MIStar instead starts with a schedule and repeatedly searches nearby alternatives to improve it.

The framework represents schedules using a heterogeneous disjunctive graph that explicitly records the ordering of operations on machines. This addresses the difficulty of representing solutions when machine assignments are flexible. A memory-enhanced graph neural network then extracts features using both the current representation and historical search trajectories, giving the decision policy information about how the search has unfolded.

MIStar combines this policy with parallel greedy search to explore alternatives and find better schedules in fewer iterations. Experiments on synthetic instances and public benchmarks show significant improvements over handcrafted improvement heuristics and leading reinforcement learning methods that construct schedules. The contribution brings representation, search history, and exploration strategy together to make iterative schedule refinement more effective in the flexible machine-allocation setting.
neurips-2025-learning-memory-enhanced-im.tldr: MIStar improves flexible job-shop schedules through graph representations, memory of past search steps, and parallel greedy exploration.

paragraphs: Activation steering controls a generative model by changing its internal activity. Fast existing approaches can align activity associated with source and target prompts, such as toxic and non-toxic text. However, locally tuned interventions do not account for their consequences in later layers, which can produce unintended changes on unfamiliar inputs.

LinEAS learns linear steering interventions with an objective that jointly accounts for distributional shifts across layers. This makes downstream effects part of the training problem. The same objective can include sparsity-promoting penalties, allowing the method to select neurons automatically. It also works with small amounts of unpaired data, without requiring explicit preference pairs.

For language-model toxicity mitigation, the authors report that LinEAS outperforms comparable approaches and becomes competitive with methods that receive strong supervision. Experiments on single-step text-to-image models also show improvements over existing activation steering methods when suppressing or introducing concepts. These findings support the value of coordinating interventions across the network while retaining a relatively lightweight way to control generation.
neurips-2025-lineas-end-to-end-learning-.tldr: LinEAS learns coordinated linear activation edits across layers to steer generation effectively from a handful of unpaired samples.

paragraphs: People affected by predictive systems may change their behavior to obtain better outcomes, especially when the system's objectives differ from their own. This paper studies users who also anticipate other users' behavior and recognize that their combined actions can change future predictions. Their decisions therefore interact through both peers and the learning system.

The authors formalize level-k thinking, in which users try to reason one step beyond their peers. Within the studied framework, this speeds convergence to equilibrium but does not change the equilibrium itself. Higher levels of individual reasoning consequently provide no lasting individual advantage in that analysis, despite changing how quickly the system settles.

The paper then considers coordinated users who optimize actions through their collective effect on the model. Comparing this behavior with selfish action reveals benefits and limits of coordination. A notion of alignment between user utilities and the learner's utility becomes central to understanding those outcomes. The analysis connects strategic behavior, feedback into future predictions, and collective action within a shared mathematical framework.
neurips-2025-look-ahead-reasoning-on-lea.tldr: The paper analyzes how anticipating peers and coordinating actions affect users' outcomes in predictive systems that learn from their behavior.

paragraphs: Turning a 3D scan into a useful CAD model requires recovering more than visible shape. Designers need a precise representation they can modify through parameters, together with the structural relationships that make those edits meaningful. Existing learning-based reconstruction methods can struggle either to produce fully parametric models or to preserve fine geometric details.

MiCADangelo takes inspiration from how human designers approach reverse engineering. It extracts cross-sections on multiple planes and uses the resulting 2D patterns to recover detailed parametric structure. This gives the reconstruction process a way to examine fine shape information through sectional views rather than relying only on a broad representation of the whole object.

The method also incorporates sketch-level constraints directly into reconstruction, an aspect the authors identify as missing from previous approaches. They report detailed, editable CAD outputs and performance exceeding existing leading methods. The contribution brings geometric detail and constrained parametric structure into the same reconstruction process, addressing the practical requirement that a recovered model should remain useful for subsequent design changes.
neurips-2025-micadangelo-fine-grained-re.tldr: MiCADangelo reconstructs detailed, editable CAD models from 3D scans using multiple cross-sections and explicit sketch constraints.

paragraphs: Reading text in video involves more than recognizing letters in a still image. Motion blur, changing appearances, and visual effects can interfere with recognition, while some questions require combining information across time. MME-VideoOCR evaluates both text reading and deeper understanding of textual content within videos.

The benchmark contains 1,464 videos and 2,000 manually annotated question-answer pairs. Its coverage includes 10 task categories, 25 tasks, and 44 scenarios, with videos varying in resolution, shape, and duration. This variety supports analysis of where models succeed or fail across different demands of video-based text understanding.

Across 18 evaluated multimodal models, the highest accuracy is 73.7%, achieved by Gemini-2.5 Pro. Models perform relatively well when relevant text appears in one or a few frames, but struggle more with holistic understanding, spatial and temporal reasoning, and combining information across frames. The analysis also identifies difficulty resisting language-based expectations. The findings emphasize the value of sufficiently detailed visual inputs and enough temporal coverage to support reliable answers about video text.
neurips-2025-mme-videoocr-evaluating-ocr.tldr: MME-VideoOCR reveals that strong text recognition in individual frames does not reliably extend to understanding text across a video.

paragraphs: Longer reasoning can improve a multimodal model's problem solving, but this paper finds that it often accompanies increased hallucination. As responses grow, models tend to move away from image-supported content and rely more heavily on language-based expectations. Attention analysis associates longer reasoning chains with reduced focus on visual inputs.

The authors introduce RH-AUC to measure how perception accuracy changes with reasoning length. This allows evaluation of whether a model remains visually grounded as it reasons. They also release RH-Bench, a diagnostic benchmark covering multiple multimodal tasks and assessing reasoning ability alongside hallucination, so that stronger reasoning scores can be considered together with perceptual reliability.

The study finds that larger models generally achieve a better balance between reasoning and perception. It also reports that training-data types and domains matter more to this balance than data volume. These are qualified empirical findings, rather than a claim that extra reasoning always harms perception. The work motivates evaluating the connection between reasoning length and visual evidence whenever extended reasoning is used to improve multimodal performance.
neurips-2025-more-thinking-less-seeing-a.tldr: Longer multimodal reasoning often weakens visual grounding, motivating a metric and benchmark that assess reasoning alongside hallucination.

paragraphs: Atmospheric forecasting requires capturing relationships across places and times. Transformers can model these broad relationships, but their complexity brings large parameter counts and lengthy training. This paper revisits the problem through atmospheric dynamics and asks how much useful structure can come from the representation of location and time itself.

The authors argue that spatial-temporal position embeddings can capture these correlations without attention mechanisms. Their explanation rests on combining geographic coordinates and temporal features that are intrinsically connected to atmospheric dynamics. STELLA uses this insight to build a forecasting model from those embeddings and a multilayer perceptron, replacing Transformer layers with a simpler architecture.

With 10,000 parameters and one hour of training, STELLA achieves better performance than other advanced methods on five datasets. These reported results show that the chosen representation can carry enough relevant structure to support strong forecasting with a small model. The paper's contribution is both architectural and conceptual: explicitly integrating spatial and temporal knowledge can reduce the need for architectural complexity in the evaluated atmospheric forecasting tasks.
neurips-2025-on-the-integration-of-spati.tldr: STELLA uses spatial-temporal embeddings and a small multilayer perceptron to achieve strong atmospheric forecasting without attention.

paragraphs: Online portfolio selection repeatedly chooses allocations to grow capital. Classical universal strategies provide long-run comparisons with a fixed rebalanced portfolio, but do not exploit forecasts. Prediction-driven heuristics can benefit from useful forecasts yet fail badly when those beliefs are wrong. This paper formalizes a setting in which predictions arrive before each allocation and may contain arbitrary errors.

The proposed Rebalanced Arithmetic Mean portfolio with predictions, or RAM, comes with two complementary guarantees under arbitrary return sequences. With perfect forecasts, it captures at least a constant fraction of hindsight-optimal wealth. Even with adversarial predictions, its wealth exceeds the geometric mean of the sequence. These guarantees describe distinct prediction conditions and distinct comparison targets.

Experiments on large equity datasets use both synthetic prediction streams and production-grade machine learning models. The authors report advantages over universal-portfolio variants that incorporate side information across several regimes. The findings support combining predictive opportunities with a fallback mathematical guarantee, rather than making the strategy's entire performance depend on forecast accuracy. The guarantees concern the stated wealth comparisons and do not assert profits in every market.
neurips-2025-online-portfolio-selection-.tldr: RAM incorporates investment forecasts while providing separate wealth guarantees for perfect and adversarial predictions.

paragraphs: Scientific drawings can reveal how students understand a phenomenon, but their free-form appearance makes automated assessment difficult. SketchMind evaluates these drawings through an explicit representation of scientific concepts and cognitive demands. Its Sketch Reasoning Graphs combine domain concepts with labels based on Bloom's taxonomy, connecting visual interpretation to educational expectations.

Separate agents handle rubric interpretation, sketch perception, cognitive alignment, and iterative feedback with sketch modification. The evaluation uses 3,575 student drawings across six science assessment items with different cognitive demands. Adding the graph representation raises GPT-4o's average accuracy from 55.6% to 77.1%, showing that the structured representation substantially improves assessment in this setting.

The authors also report further benefits from coordinating multiple agents, including an average 8.9% increase in prediction accuracy with GPT-4.1. Human evaluators rate that system's feedback and co-created sketches at 4.1 out of 5, compared with 2.3 for a GPT-4o baseline. Experts identify potential for supporting conceptual growth through guided revision. These results support the assessment and feedback approach, while the educational-growth claim remains a stated potential.
neurips-2025-sketchmind-a-multi-agent-co.tldr: SketchMind combines concept graphs and specialized agents to improve assessment and revision feedback for student scientific drawings.

paragraphs: Sparse linear bandits model repeated decisions in settings with many possible dimensions but a sparse underlying structure. An algorithm must balance immediate reward with learning what makes an action valuable. Existing methods commonly target either abundant-data settings or scarce-data settings, where the best achievable dependence on dimension and the number of rounds differs.

Bayesian Information Directed Sampling can achieve optimal regret rates in both regimes simultaneously, but its guarantee relies on Bayesian assumptions. This paper develops Sparse Optimistic Information Directed Sampling to obtain corresponding worst-case guarantees without those assumptions. Regret measures the performance lost through the sequence of decisions, making it the central quantity for comparing the approaches.

The analysis enables a learning rate that changes over time and shows how the information-versus-regret balance can be tuned without prior knowledge. The authors establish an algorithm with optimal worst-case regret in both data regimes simultaneously and report good empirical performance. The theoretical contribution is therefore adaptation across the two regimes while moving beyond the Bayesian setting in which the earlier combined guarantee was available.
neurips-2025-sparse-optimistic-informati.tldr: SOIDS achieves optimal worst-case regret in both data-rich and data-poor sparse linear bandits without Bayesian assumptions.

paragraphs: Agents acting from visual and language instructions need to understand goals, plan across several steps, and respond to changing environments. Directly mapping inputs to actions can make those demands difficult to handle. ThinkAct introduces a dual-system design that connects explicit high-level reasoning with a separate model responsible for executing actions.

A multimodal language model learns to produce embodied reasoning plans using reinforcement signals tied to visual evidence of goal completion and trajectory consistency. The plans are compressed into a visual latent representation, which conditions the downstream action model. This intermediate representation provides a connection between the reasoning process and the actions carried out in the target environment.

Experiments on embodied reasoning and robot manipulation benchmarks demonstrate few-shot adaptation, planning over long horizons, and self-correction behavior. The contribution is the combination of planning rewards aligned with action outcomes and a compact representation that carries plans into execution. The reported behaviors indicate that this connection can help agents handle complex tasks requiring more than a direct response to the current input.
neurips-2025-thinkact-vision-language-ac.tldr: ThinkAct links reinforced multimodal reasoning plans to action execution through a compact visual representation.

paragraphs: Spatial video grounding locates an object across video frames from a language instruction. Drone footage introduces moving viewpoints and complex aerial scenes that existing grounding tasks have underexplored. This paper defines spatial aerial video grounding and introduces UAV-SVG, a benchmark with more than two million frames and 216 target categories.

The proposed SAVG-DETR model handles multiple visual scales by separating two computations: language-image interaction within each scale and visual fusion across scales. This avoids the attention cost of processing every interaction together. A language modulation component incorporates information from multiple scales, while progressive decoding increasingly uses lower-level visual-language features to improve grounding of small objects.

To maintain consistency across frames, the decoder predicts offsets from reference anchors and updates those anchors at successive stages. This progressively narrows and refines the object's location until it produces the spatial tube, the object's sequence of localized regions through the video. Experiments report significant improvements over existing leading methods. The architecture addresses aerial grounding through coordinated changes to scale handling, small-object decoding, and repeated localization refinement.
neurips-2025-where-does-it-exist-from-th.tldr: UAV-SVG and SAVG-DETR advance language-guided object localization in drone videos through a large benchmark and progressive multiscale grounding.

paragraphs: Central-bank communications convey policy information whose interpretation can have important economic consequences. This paper introduces the World Central Banks dataset to support consistent analysis across institutions. It contains more than 380,000 sentences from 25 central banks across geographically diverse regions and spans 28 years of communications.

The authors sample 1,000 sentences per bank across the available years, producing 25,000 annotated sentences. Each receives labels for policy stance, temporal classification, and uncertainty. Annotation uses two annotators, disagreement resolution, and secondary expert review. The resulting tasks provide several complementary ways to examine what a communication says and how it expresses its message.

The benchmark evaluates seven pretrained language models and nine large language models under several prompting conditions. A central finding is that training on pooled data from multiple banks significantly outperforms training on one bank's data. Human evaluations, error analyses, and predictive tasks further support the framework's economic usefulness. The results indicate that information shared across institutions can improve interpretation, giving the combined corpus value beyond separate bank-specific collections.
neurips-2025-words-that-unite-the-world-.tldr: The WCB dataset supports unified analysis of central-bank language and shows benefits from training across banks.
